Derive null, negative and positive controls from a table

Source: R/controls.R
controls.Rd

Builds the control datasets a control_spec() declares, from any table with a role table: a synthetic clone, a comparator's clone, or, on the owner's side, the original. Nothing is re-simulated. Three kinds of control exist, each with a known truth:

Usage

controls(df, roles, spec = NULL, events = NULL, seed = NULL, recipe = NULL)

Arguments

df

The table to derive controls from: a data frame or data.table.

roles

Its role table, as returned by roles() for a clone or by propose_roles() and set_role() for any table. Or a plan: the analyst passes clone_plan() with the clone, the owner passes the plan and the recipe with the real table.

spec

A control_spec(). With a plan in roles, the name of one of its specs, or NULL when it holds exactly one.

events

Linked time/status pairs among the outcome columns, in the form mask() takes. The null permutes each pair as one block. NULL when there are none.

seed

A private integer seed for the permutations that overrides the spec's seed, for the owner's side; NULL uses the spec's seed, or with a recipe the recipe's key. A value equal to the spec's seed is refused there. See "Two sides, two seeds" for what an integer can and cannot hide.

recipe

With a plan in roles, the recipe of the clone. df is then the real table: its cleaning and conformance are replayed as in apply_recipe(), a table with a different schema, NA mask or values is refused, and a spec that differs from the one fixed at mask() is refused.

Value

A masque_controls object: the resolved spec (@spec), the manifest (@manifest, one row per dataset), the truth table (@truth, one row per target and level of on) and the notes (@notes). Datasets are produced by control_table().

Details

  • null: every analysed column (outcome, covariate and date columns with action scramble or alias) is permuted independently over its non-missing rows; a column declared unit-grained is permuted across its units and stays constant within each. Design, treatment and kept columns, the NA mask and every column's multiset of values are kept. No association among analysed columns, or with the treatment, remains. Use it as a smoke test: a pipeline that finds signal here builds that signal itself. A leak already in the table, such as a covariate that copies the outcome, is shuffled away with the rest and passes.

  • negative: the declared column on alone is permuted within the declared design strata, at its unit, while the design structure and all other associations are kept. The outcome is not changed, so any real effect of on stays in it as unexplained variation. Choose strata that every level of on can reach. Complete replicates qualify. Within incomplete blocks each block keeps its set of levels, so part of the real effect of on survives. With n replicates it gives a permutation null for a whole pipeline: a false-positive rate, a permutation p-value.

  • positive: the same permutation as the negative replicate, plus the declared shift per level of on on each target, in units of the target's standard deviation in the table at hand. Positive minus negative is the planted truth, exactly.

Declaration before data

The spec is resolved against the table here: on defaults to the single treatment column; strata and unit are checked for nesting; an effect given as list(sd = ) is drawn under the spec's seed, once, so the same spec plants the same vector on every table it meets. The resolved spec and the truth table are on the returned object and in its print.

Two sides, two seeds

An analyst who holds only the clone runs this on the clone. The owner runs it on the original, offline, on a private draw (the planted vector still comes from the spec's seed). A public seed would let anyone who knows the design, which the clone shares, rebuild every permutation and read the original outcome out of per-replicate statistics.

With a plan and its recipe, the permutations come from SHA-256 of a 256-bit key the recipe holds, so there is no seed to search. A private integer seed is the weaker route: it has at most 31 bits, and anyone given a per-replicate statistic can try each value, because the true seed fits the statistic exactly and a wrong one does not.

Control tables built from an original never leave the owner. What may leave goes through the owner's usual output checking, classed by what it estimates. The false-positive rate says little about the real outcome. The rate at which the positives find the shift depends on the residual variance. The permutation p-value is the result of the analyst's test on the real table. A vector of per-replicate means or contrasts is not an aggregate, under either route, and every further pipeline run on the original is another set of queries.

Limits

A kept column is structure and is never permuted, so leakage through kept columns, ids or row order passes the null. No control can detect confounding. A planted effect is clean: uniform within a level, with no confounding and no interaction. Nothing is clipped, so a shift can take a non-negative outcome below zero; control_table() warns when it does. The null collapses the design means of row-grained outcomes, so false-positive calibration comes from the negative control, not the null.

A negative control is a test of the stated size for a comparison that uses only contrasts within the strata, so the analysis needs the strata in its model. Permuting within replicates and fitting no replicate term puts the replicate variance in the residual and rejects far less often than the nominal level. A shared rate on the clone and the original shows that the two agree, and a rate of zero on both says nothing about calibration. A warning (class masque_control_unit_small) marks units and strata with too few arrangements for a 5 percent level, and another (class masque_control_strata_weak) marks strata that hold one level of on.

See also

control_spec(), control_table(), mask(), roles().

Examples

trial <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "john_alpha.csv", package = "masque"))
r <- propose_roles(trial, detect = FALSE)
r <- set_role(r, c("rep", "block"), role = "design", action = "keep")
r <- set_role(r, "gen", role = "treatment", action = "keep")
r <- set_role(r, "yield", role = "outcome", action = "scramble")
r <- set_role(r, c("plot", "row", "col"), role = "id", action = "keep")
spec <- control_spec(
  on = "gen", target = "yield", effect = list(sd = 0.5),
  strata = "rep", n = 5L, seed = 2026L
)
ctl <- controls(trial, r, spec)
ctl
